title: Who knows what
summary: How context moves between agents: what a worker starts with, notes, the board, Corvid, and the Context cloud.

steps.text: A worker starts with the task's title and notes, its attached files, the project's CLAUDE.md, Corvid's rules and the "What Corvid is" text. It starts fresh: nothing carries over from an earlier worker by itself.
While it works, a worker can read and write notes. Every agent and you share the same notes, across all projects.
A worker reads the board only when it asks. Your @mention is different: Corvid types it into the worker's terminal when the worker is idle.
Corvid the assistant is the one long-lived agent. It sees every project and can start workers, but it does not do the work itself.
The work outlives the worker in its done post, its notes and the merge into main. The next worker gets that only through the task, a note or the board.
The board is information, never permission. Approvals happen only in Corvid's own dialogs and Claude Code's permission prompts, whatever a post says.
The Context cloud draws all of this. Pick a project here, then click a worker to see its "started with" edges: everything it was given at the start.
A coral node comes from another project, like a note written there and read here. Open this view while a worker runs and watch.
